text:
sasha: Hey team — customer says their free trial was blocked when they tried to apply promo code TRIAL50. Account acct_01G7x, email mike.p@gmail.com. They claim they're using Azure Cloud Shell to test and say it's a legit dev. Can someone take a look?

liam: I'm on it. Quick checks: ip 13.68.45.21 flagged as Azure CloudShell / Microsoft ASN, email domain gmail (looks normal) but our disposable-email check returned true? odd. Do we have the fraud flags for that account?

sasha: Pasting the risk summary from the fraud service:```
account: acct_01G7x
ip: 13.68.45.21
ip_risk: high
vpn_score: 0.82
email_domain_disposable: true
phone_verified: false
promo_attempts: 1
user_agent: "Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) Azure-CloudShell/1.0"
```

dev-bot: Automated risk note: suspicious_device=true; high_cloud_provider_ip=true; disposable_email_hit=1; recommended_action=manual_review

liam: OK disposable_email probably a false positive — gmail shouldn't be disposable. Looks like our disposable regex matched something weird (common with gmail+alias patterns?). I'll pull the full email tokenization and domain checks.

maya: If it's Cloud Shell + high vpn_score we usually expect higher fraud rates, but if the user is a legit dev on CloudShell we can manual-grant. Ask them for a quick verification (screenshot of dashboard + confirm org/repo) or phone last4. If they provide that, we can grant a trial override. :white_check_mark:

noah: Also note that Cloud Shell IPs are ephemeral and can be shared; we should avoid a blanket allowlist for Microsoft ASNs. For a one-off manual grant that's fine. If we see repeated promo abuse from the same ASN we can revisit.

liam: Repro steps I used to trigger same flag from my end (using Azure Cloud Shell):
```bash
# open azure cloud shell, then run:
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/promos/apply \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" \
  -H "User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) Azure-CloudShell/1.0" \
  -d '{"account_id":"acct_01G7x","promo":"TRIAL50"}'
```
response: 403 {"error":"trial_onhold","reason":"risk_flags:ip_risk,vpn_score,email_disposable"}

liam: I can strip debug logs and post safe excerpt to support ticket. Recommend manual-review + flag temporary whitelist for this account if verification provided.

maya: Sasha — ask customer to reply in ticket with one of: (a) photo of company email domain control / work email, (b) last4 of phone used for billing, or (c) a screenshot of a public repo or company page showing they're with the startup. If they supply, we'll do a 14-day trial grant and add note to the account: "manual grant 14d — verified via screenshot".

sasha: Requested verification from customer in ticket. They replied with screenshot of their internal dashboard and a GitHub repo link. I pasted both into the ticket.

liam: Verified screenshot timestamps and repo — small startup, looks fine. I'm going to run a manual grant. Admin command:```
# admin console (internal)
POST /internal/admin/grant_trial
{ "account_id":"acct_01G7x", "duration_days":14, "reason":"manual_verification_screenshot_github", "actor":"liam" }
```
Executing now.

dev-bot: Action logged: admin.grant_trial acct_01G7x by liam at 1998456205; duration=14d; note=manual_verification_screenshot_github

maya: Please also add a short note on the account and tag fraud for a light follow-up in 10 days to ensure there's no abuse. Noah, can infra add a short-term safe-pass for this account so our promo flow doesn't re-block while they use the trial? Should be scoped to account_id only.

noah: Yep, I added an account-scoped bypass rule (expires in 14d) — rule id bypass_199845. Doesn't affect global checks.

liam: Left a manual review record and set follow-up reminder. Will monitor promo_attempts and IP churn.

sasha: Customer notified and says trial is active now. Thanks everyone. Closing this thread — tagging for audit: @fraud-team FYI. :tada:

maya: Thanks — good call on manual verification, looks clean. We'll avoid adding CloudShell to any ASNs allowlist for now.

noah: Noted — filing a short doc for how to handle Cloud Shell cases in the fraud runbook so next time it's faster.

sasha: Closing.
